auth: Requires a Bearer token. Every endpoint here is documented against the solo owner (role `owner`, acting in a Staff-style capacity — see business-owner.md's S1/S2 stories) since that's the only fulfillment session built so far; Phase 5's Front Desk/Staff roles will extend this same domain, not replace it.

endpoints.description: Fetches bookings for a business. Supports optional `date` (single day, for Today), `from`/`to` (range, for Calendar's month view and Earnings), and `status` query params. Today/Calendar/Earnings currently all read from one client-side array that only ever holds bookings created during the current app session — a real backend needs this endpoint to actually list bookings that already existed, not just ones the app itself just created.

endpoints.screen: New appointment — Now (business-owner app, Today tab "+")
endpoints.description: Records a walk-in: the customer is already physically present, so this skips pending_payment/confirmed entirely and starts life as in_progress — no deposit, no date/time picking (server should stamp the current date/time, not trust a client-sent one). customerName falls back to "Walk-in customer" client-side if left blank; customerPhone/customerEmail are optional. staffId is optional too — null/omitted means unassigned ("Any available"/"Walk-in"); when present it's a team.json add-team-member invitationId, which is how a member's earnings view (see get-earnings-summary) knows which bookings are theirs.

errors.message: services must include at least one item

endpoints.screen: New appointment — Schedule (business-owner app, Calendar tab "+", or a customer's "New appointment" button)
endpoints.description: Owner manually books a future appointment on someone's behalf. Same shape as create-walk-in-booking (including the optional staffId assignment) plus date/time, and starts life as confirmed rather than in_progress — the owner still has to check the customer in (see update-booking-status) when they actually arrive. Uses source `walk_in` (owner-recorded) rather than a separate value, since the only real difference from a walk-in is the starting status.

endpoints.description: Drives Appointment Detail's status stepper: check-in (confirmed → in_progress), no-show, and cancel. (in_progress → completed happens via charge-booking below, not this endpoint, since completing always goes through a payment record.)

errors.message: Cannot move from completed to in_progress

endpoints.description: Records the final service charge once a booking is in_progress, and marks it completed. `method` is `mpesa` (sends an STK push to `customerPhone` through the business's connected payment destination — request must include customerPhone) or `cash` (no phone needed, records instantly). Separate from confirm-booking-payment, which is the customer-facing up-front deposit push at booking time, not this after-the-fact full charge. `paymentReference` is the M-Pesa receipt number once paid via mpesa (null for cash — there's no receipt for cash); shown in Appointment Detail's Payment card and is what 'txn details from mpesa' on the Transactions list drills into.

errors.message: customerPhone is required when method is mpesa

endpoints.description: Revenue trend buckets, payment-method breakdown, per-service breakdown, per-transaction ledger, and appointment counts for a date range (`from`/`to` query params, both 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Also takes an optional `staffId` query param — when present, scopes every number to bookings assigned to that team member (see create-walk-in-booking's staffId), which is what TeamMemberDetailScreen's earnings section needs; omitted, it's the whole-business view EarningsScreen shows. Mirrors what src/utils/earnings.ts currently computes client-side by filtering every booking in memory — fine for mock data, not something a real backend should do at scale. `services` should include every service the business currently offers, not just ones with revenue (bookingsCount: 0 rows included) — both screens use that to show what isn't selling, not just what is. `transactions` is one row per service actually performed (not per booking), newest first — the client caps this at 10 for preset ranges and shows everything for a custom range, so a real backend could paginate rather than always returning every row, but the mock returns the full set and lets the client slice it. Only bookings with paymentStatus 'paid' count toward any amount here.

endpoints.description: Creates or updates a customer record entered through the walk-in/schedule flow. `customerId` present means the client already matched this to an existing customer (by phone — the closest thing to a stable identifier the app has) and this is an update to their name/email; absent means create a new one.

Lists this business's saved customers. No mock implementation exists yet (see src/api/customers.ts) — CustomersScreen currently only ever shows customers saved during the current app session via save-customer, since there's no fetch-on-mount, same as every other post-publish store in this app.

endpoints.description: Staff requests a withdrawal from their earnings wallet (staff.md's S3, wallet model — the balance accumulates continuously as bookings get charged, not a fixed once-a-day amount; see types/payout.ts). `amount` can be anything up to their available balance (lifetime commission earned minus everything already requested with status 'pending' or 'paid' — a 'rejected' request releases its amount back) — the client computes and enforces this, but a real backend must re-check it server-side, not trust the client. Always comes back 'pending' — see respond-to-payout for how the owner moves it to 'paid'/'rejected'.

endpoints.screen: Team — Payouts queue / Payout history (business-owner app)
endpoints.description: Lists payout requests for a business, optionally filtered by `status` (e.g. `?status=pending` for the Team tab's queue). No mock implementation exists yet (see src/api/payouts.ts) — TeamScreen/PayoutHistoryScreen currently read usePayoutsStore's client-side array directly, same 'no fetch-on-mount' pattern every other post-publish store in this app already uses (list-customers has the same gap, for the same reason).

endpoints.screen: Payout Detail — Accept & send / Reject (business-owner app)
endpoints.description: Owner approves or rejects a pending payout request. `action: 'approve'` is a manual attestation that the owner has already sent the money themselves (M-Pesa/cash) — Trimyy has no real payment rail, so this never moves money, it only records that a human did. `action: 'reject'` takes an optional `rejectionReason`, shown back to the staff member on their own payout history and released back into their available wallet balance.
